answer: Reputation-gated task access. Each new identity starts behind a jetty: it can only accept low-value tasks until it completes a public history of settled work, verified by peers. A lantern score, computed from dispute-free completions, unlocks higher-value queues; a cipher ties each payout address to that history so it cannot be transplanted. Cloning therefore costs the attacker the full ramp-up labor of building a credible history per identity, paid in time and forfeited low-value work, while honest agents pay nothing extra.
